reason: The Hebrew people explicitly express discontent with their leaders' absence. Upon seeing Moses has delayed coming down from Mount Sinai, they gather to Aaron and demand (ויאמרו אליו קום עשה לנו אלהים): 'Make us gods who will go before us, because this Moses—the man who brought us up from Egypt—we do not know what has become of him.' This represents active dissatisfaction with their leadership, specifically complaining about Moses's prolonged absence and demanding that Aaron create a replacement deity. The people's lack of confidence in their leaders' ability to guide them further demonstrates clear complaint about leadership.
